claim: A fresh GitHub-hosted runner passed seven unchanged upstream restic tests, then checked and restored two exact synthetic snapshots using a password delivered separately from the published ciphertext; independent review reconciled the returned outputs, file manifests and platform record.
limitations: Synthetic byte/POSIX-mode recovery only, not ai-memory/Qdrant application-state recovery, reboot, production disaster recovery, lost-password recovery or provider savings.
The ciphertext and separate protected secret share a GitHub administrative account; account-loss recovery and independent trust domains are not established.
The seven selected upstream tests are a focused subset, not the entire upstream suite. Our transfer fixture and complete-file oracle are explicitly local integration checks.
UID/GID restoration, timestamps, ACL/xattrs, sparse files, links, Windows filesystems and long-term storage availability were not qualified.
Interface inventory is unavailable; distinct native network/mount namespaces and frozen read-only bindings are the observed isolation properties.

Two restore banners replace the source username with $SOURCE_USER; their original raw hashes cannot be recomputed from the sanitized public text. Other declared stream hashes were independently checked.

native_returns.operation: restore snapshot 2 with an invalid password
native_returns.stderr: Fatal: wrong password or no key found

independent_review.method: Read-only reviewer independently fetched the GitHub artifact, compared all native streams and restored manifests with the frozen source and a separate fixture oracle, and checked platform job records; no native restore rerun or secret access.
